description: The image displays a concentric (doughnut-style) pie chart comparing two categories labeled “Ambiguity” (outer ring) and “Ambiguity 2 (Inner)” (inner ring), each segmented into three response types: “Deceived” (red), “Partially” (yellow), and “Not Deceived” (green), as indicated by two identical legends. The outer “Ambiguity” ring shows 67.6% “Deceived” (red), 31.6% “Partially” (yellow), and 10.5% “Not Deceived” (green). The inner “Ambiguity 2 (Inner)” ring shows 57.9% “Deceived” (red), 23.5% “Partially” (yellow), and 8.8% “Not Deceived” (green). The chart visually emphasizes that across both ambiguity conditions, the “Deceived” category dominates, followed by “Partially,” with “Not Deceived” being the smallest segment in both rings. The percentages are displayed directly on the corresponding segments, and the color coding is consistent between the two rings, allowing for direct comparison of proportions across the two ambiguity conditions.
